title: Premium Payment Conditions for Homeowners Insurance
content:
**Premium due.** The premium due on a Homeowners Insurance policy is the premium and policy fees billed to the insured and not yet paid or credited back. Each bill line carries a bill number printed on the premium notice, in the form HSB-778120-03, and a due date.

**Installments.** The term premium is billed in equal installments under the payment plan the insured chose from the plans the HomeShield program offers. The last installment absorbs any rounding cent.

**Installment fee.** Every installment after the first carries the program's installment fee, billed as its own installment fee line.

**Payment methods.** Payments are made by one of the program's payment methods.

**Application of payments.** A payment is applied to the oldest open bill line first.

**Late fee.** An installment paid after its due date carries the program's late fee.

## Illustrations (hypothetical figures)

**Equal installments and the rounding cent.** A term premium of 1,000.01 dollars on the quarterly plan is billed as four installments: 250.00, 250.00, 250.00 and, absorbing the rounding cent, 250.01 dollars. The second, third and fourth installments each also carry an installment fee line.

**Oldest line first.** An insured has two open bill lines: an installment billed and due in one month, and an installment with its installment fee line billed and due in the following month. A payment received is applied first to the earlier month's installment, the oldest open line, and only what remains goes to the later lines.

**Late fee boundary, on abstract days.** An installment paid on its due date is not paid after its due date. An installment paid on any day after its due date carries the late fee.

## Basis Q&A

**Does the first installment carry an installment fee?**
No. The installment fee applies to every installment after the first.

**Can one installment differ from the others?**
Only the last one, which absorbs any rounding cent left by dividing the term premium into equal installments.

**What does a payment pay first?**
The oldest open bill line.
